constraints.statement: Backend-neutral contracts and registries already exist for every knowledge plane (ontology: `register_ontology_backend`; GraphIndex: `register_graph_backend`; wiki: `register_wiki_backend`; source manifest: `SourceManifestBackend`).
constraints.implication: a replacement is a set of registrations into these seams; the draft's parallel `OntologyStore` / `KnowledgeStore` Protocols and its decision D7 would duplicate shipped FEAT-540 work

constraints.statement: The traversal contract is dialect-bound: a store exposes `dialect`, `execute_pattern` needs a template in that dialect or raises `TraversalPatternUnavailable`, and `execute_query` rejects a `DynamicQuery` in another dialect.
constraints.implication: a non-AQL backend serves nothing until every pattern has a template in its dialect (or a neutral traversal spec exists) and a validator is registered for that dialect

constraints.statement: AQL is ontology content, not only store code: bundled `*.ontology.yaml` patterns, ArangoSearch `search_views`, the LLM dynamic-query path and the validators are all AQL; tenant/client YAML outside the repository carries more.
constraints.implication: the migration has a content track (re-template patterns, re-prompt the dynamic path, map search views to another FTS index) that the draft does not mention

constraints.statement: The coded ontology is a layered YAML property-graph schema plus a per-tenant instance graph (employees, norms, contracts, procedures) with discovery, refresh and authorization reachability — there is no RDF, Turtle, SKOS or IRI anywhere, and `rdflib` / `pyshacl` are undeclared.
constraints.implication: the draft's OntologyStore (concept vocabulary + closure) is a different, greenfield object; it does not replace what `parrot.knowledge.ontology` does today

constraints.statement: Tenancy is one graph database plus one pgvector schema per tenant, and `TenantContext.arango_db` is a required field of the context every contract method takes.
constraints.implication: the new backend needs a per-tenant isolation unit and the field must be generalised; the draft's `ontology_id` / namespace axis is a different partitioning

constraints.statement: The concept vocabulary is already authoritative in Postgres (`ontology_concept*` tables, five-state machine, outbox); ArangoDB only receives a materialised copy, and concept embeddings live in pgvector table `ontology.concepts`.
constraints.implication: the Postgres half of the draft partly exists under another schema; the work is removing the Arango materialisation and adding what patterns need (is_a expansion), and `CREATE SCHEMA ontology` would collide with `ontology.concepts`

constraints.statement: A Postgres server plane already ships for GraphIndex and for the wiki (FEAT-520): asyncpg only, no SQLAlchemy, no `PgVectorStore` reuse, bitemporal append-only versioning, `ts_rank_cd` judged sufficient over true BM25, fresh ingests only.
constraints.implication: removing ArangoDB from GraphIndex and the wiki is a deletion plus data move, not a new backend; the draft's rejection of plain Postgres for the wiki reverses a recorded decision and must be justified

constraints.statement: Seven modules import `ArangoOntologyGraphStore` directly (refresh, concept catalog reconcile/worker, the legal/BOE pack in ai-parrot-tools) and the public package exports it.
constraints.implication: the concrete class cannot be deleted until these are typed against the contracts; this spans two distributions

constraints.statement: ArangoDB is also used outside the knowledge planes: an Arango vector store, the `arangodbsearch` tool, `parrot/interfaces/hierarchy.py`, a formdesigner sink, routing rules and the contracts/manuals loaders — 43 files in four distributions.
constraints.implication: "ArangoDB must be removed" is larger than the draft's scope; the feature has to state which of these it covers

constraints.statement: Database access goes through `asyncdb`, and the installed asyncdb ships no SurrealDB driver; `surrealdb` is declared in no `pyproject.toml`.
constraints.implication: a SurrealDB store needs the raw SDK (a new dependency and extra) or a new asyncdb driver

constraints.statement: The ontology RAG path degrades to `vector_only` when the graph is unavailable.
constraints.implication: the new backend must keep failing soft; a pattern with no template in the new dialect must degrade, not crash

constraints.statement: Approved FEAT-670 adds HelixDB to the same planes and states ArangoDB is not retired; FEAT-540 states ArangoDB keeps working unchanged; no ADR, decision page or commit records the licence decision — the reasoning exists only in an untracked research note.
constraints.implication: the removal needs an ADR that cites the research note and supersedes those positions; FEAT-670 is superseded (user decision U1)

constraints.statement: Bookstore and PageIndex are canonical on SQLite and files; FEAT-670 had decided projection-only for them, and the L1 synthesis cache has no persistence today.
constraints.implication: moving Bookstore and L1 to SurrealDB is re-platforming unrelated to the ArangoDB removal

constraints.statement: Engine selection criteria, stated by the user and backed by the research note: open-source, non-enterprise editions only; no paid SaaS; must run on the AWS services in use (Apache AGE is not installable on Amazon RDS); and the platform must get simpler, so multi-service stacks such as JanusGraph (Cassandra plus Elasticsearch) are out.
constraints.implication: any backend proposed in the spec is checked against these four criteria; they also explain why the note's first choice (PostgreSQL + AGE) is not the one adopted

risks.statement: Scope: the four answers make this a multi-feature programme (new ontology model, new knowledge store, port of every consumer, workspace-wide removal, data migration); one spec and one worktree will not hold it.

SurrealDB is documented but untested here: the research note records BM25, HNSW, RRF and multi-process server mode, and also that the Python SDK 3.x is beta and transactions exist only over WebSocket; spike G1 must run before anything else. It is BSL 1.1 (source-available, not OSI): unlike ArangoDB there is no restrictive binary licence, but users who offer it as a service carry that obligation.

The draft's OntologyStore does not cover what the ontology subsystem does today; with ArangoDB gone everywhere, the instance graph, traversal patterns, dynamic queries, refresh and authorization reachability need a destination in the same programme (U5).

Two concept authorities would coexist: the reviewed, tenant-scoped Postgres concept catalog and the Turtle-published, IRI-keyed OntologyStore; the draft's single `ontology_id` axis has no slot for per-tenant overlays.

Model mismatch on the knowledge side: the wiki contract is page-level (`BaseWikiStore`: pages, edges, embeddings, sources, meta, compare-and-swap, federation), Bookstore is PageIndex trees, L1 is section-level; the draft's bundle/document/section/chunk schema matches none of them one-to-one.

Recorded decisions are reversed without a record: FEAT-520 judged Postgres FTS sufficient for the wiki and chose fresh ingests only, FEAT-540 kept ArangoDB working unchanged, FEAT-670 kept Bookstore/PageIndex canonical on files.
AQL written by tenants and generated by the LLM lives outside the repository's control; a dialect change needs a content migration and a new safety validator.
No migration tooling exists for any ArangoDB plane.
Sequencing with FEAT-541 (GraphIndex package extraction, spec'd, not implemented) and the unmerged `feat-255-ontology-rag-kb` branch, which touch the same seams.
House convention is database access through asyncdb, which has no SurrealDB driver; the raw SDK is a deliberate exception.

The adopted engine is the research note's third choice; the first (PostgreSQL + AGE) is excluded by Amazon RDS and the second (FalkorDB) by SSPL, per-graph write serialisation and no BM25. The note also recommends keeping ArangoDB as an optional legacy adapter, while the user chose removal from the whole workspace — the removal should be the last phase, after parity.
